quiz_plan.promise: the quiz plays the page's promise: a skin type quiz a visitor can take, whose results answer what the H1 says it builds

plan.angle: The top 10 is skincare brands and health publishers running their own skin type quizzes, with no builder in it. A visitor can take an eight-question skin type quiz on this page and get one of five skin types (normal, dry, oily, combination, or sensitive), then see what four businesses do with a result: a facial studio sets up the first appointment, a subscription box swaps a moisturizer after an October retake, a skincare brand picks its next launch from the counts, and a grooming brand runs the quiz from a code on the box. Every result lands in a database the owner keeps. The FAQ covers the Fitzpatrick and Baumann systems, free quizzes, question count, scoring, and when to send people to a dermatologist.
tab_stories: Linden Row Skin Studio sends the skin type quiz with every first-facial booking, and Hana Whitlock's Sensitive result books the 50-minute calming facial and emails esthetician Ines Corrado before Thursday's appointment.
Fairmoor Box asks every subscriber to retake the quiz each October, and Priya Lund's result moves from Oily to Combination, so her November box swaps the gel moisturizer for the lotion.
Wrenhaven Skincare counts 2,400 finished quizzes over the spring, Combination leads with 860, and the product team picks a combination-skin moisturizer as the next launch.
Ridgeback Grooming prints a code on every box that opens the quiz on a phone, one question per screen, and Tomasz Reyes lands on Oily with the line's foaming cleanser named on his result.

claims_to_source: The five skin types are normal, dry, oily, combination, and sensitive
Skin type can change over time, and oiliness changes with the time of year or the weather
Combination skin is dry or normal in some areas and oily in others, such as the T-zone
The Fitzpatrick scale classifies skin by how it reacts to the sun (tendency to burn or tan), in six types
The Baumann system sorts skin into 16 types from four pairs: dry or oily, sensitive or resistant, pigmented or non-pigmented, and wrinkle-prone or tight
A dermatologist or an aesthetician at a skincare counter can help choose products
